title: The per-lane host bubble is painted BEHIND the modal 'Go online?' popup, so no one can read which hosts a lane contacts
repro: Boot in airplane mode (the default), click the filled plane icon (#net-toggle), rest the mouse on any lane name under 'Where this will let the app connect:' (e.g. 'Law').
expected: A bubble appears ON TOP of the popup next to the mouse with that lane's hosts, transport sentence and any always-on / discarded-switch sentence (Q1002: 'its hover lists, per lane, the hosts that lane will contact'; invariant #17).
actual: Nothing appears. #oo-tip gets class 'show', opacity 1 and the right text, but it renders under the dialog. There are 0 changed pixels in the bubble's box on all 15 lanes in en, fr and zh (retried with a 1.5 s rest). The same bubble outside a dialog changes 73% of its box. In ar the bubble starts at the right-aligned lane, so only its part past the popup's right edge shows, dimmed by the ::backdrop and cut off at the dialog edge. The native title tooltip is suppressed too, because show() strips the title.
evidence: Screenshots /tmp/claude-0/walk/H/H-H3-en-law-hover.png, H-H3-en-press-hover.png, H-H3-en-custody-hover-1500ms.png, H-H7-ar-wiki-hover.png; pixel diffs in part1.json (H3[].diff_whole_tip), part2.json (H3_retry), part3.json (hover_checks); control part1.json H1.tip_on_plane_pixel_diff. Cause: src/static/app-core.js:1325 opens #net-consent with dlg.showModal(), which puts it in the top layer; src/static/app-boot.js:259-267 appends #oo-tip to <body>; src/static/app.css:1793 gives it only position:fixed; z-index:400, which cannot rise above the top layer; src/static/app-boot.js:280 removes the title on show. The earlier sandbox walks could not catch this: one used is_visible(), the other read textContent.
root_cause: src/static/app-core.js:1325 opens #net-consent with dlg.showModal(), which puts it in the browser top layer. src/static/app-boot.js:259-267 creates #oo-tip and appends it to <body>. src/static/app.css:1793 gives it only position:fixed; z-index:400, and no z-index can rise above the top layer. src/static/app-boot.js:281 removes the element's title on show(), so the native tooltip cannot stand in either. The 2026-09-16 sandbox record (docs/audit/net-consent-hosts-2026-09-16/clickthrough.py:89-90) used locator.is_visible(), which does not detect top-layer occlusion.
suggested_fix: In ooTipInit's show() (app-boot.js ~line 279), host the bubble in the top-most open modal that contains the hovered element before showing it: `const host = el.closest('dialog[open]') || document.body; if (tip.parentElement !== host) host.appendChild(tip);`. hide() needs no change, and moving the bubble back to <body> on hide is optional. The alternative is to make #oo-tip a manual popover (tip.popover='manual'; tip.showPopover() in show(), hidePopover() in hide()), so it enters the top layer above the dialog. Add a Chromium regression that checks elementFromPoint at the bubble's centre, or a pixel check, instead of is_visible().

title: Lane names in the consent popup cannot take keyboard focus, so their host bubble has no keyboard path
repro: Open the 'Go online?' popup, press Tab repeatedly.
expected: Each lane name is focusable, and focus opens its #oo-tip bubble (invariant #17: 'opens … on hover, keyboard focus, or touch long-press').
actual: All 15 lane spans have tabIndex -1. Tab cycles Go online > body > #net-consent-body > Stay offline > Go online and never reaches a lane.
evidence: part1.json H3_lane_focusable and H3_tab_sequence; src/static/app-core.js:1237-1246 (_laneLine renders a plain <span title=…> with no tabindex). The fix for the P1 would need to cover this path too.
root_cause: src/static/app-core.js:1246 (_laneLine) renders `<span title=...>` with no tabindex. src/static/app-boot.js:269-273 (mark) adds .oo-tip-target but never makes the element focusable.
suggested_fix: Add tabindex="0" to the lane span in _laneLine (app-core.js:1246). Together with the P1 fix, the existing focusin handler then opens the bubble inside the dialog. An app-wide fix would have mark() add tabindex=0 to non-focusable .oo-tip-target elements, but that is a larger change to the focus order.

title: Arabic (RTL): '*.wikipedia.org' in the Wikipedia lane bubble is broken; its '*.' jumps to the far end of the line
repro: Switch to العربية, open the popup, hover 'ويكيبيديا / ويكيميديا' and look at the part of the bubble that shows past the popup's right edge.
expected: Each host reads left to right as one intact token ('*.wikipedia.org').
actual: The line reads 'wikipedia.org · stream.wikimedia.org ·.*': the leading '*.' is placed at the right-hand end by the RTL bidi algorithm.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/H/H-H7-ar-wiki-hover-zoom.png, H-H7-ar-wiki-hover.png. The host list is joined as plain text (src/static/app-core.js:1218-1234, _laneHostTitle) and rendered as textContent in an RTL #oo-tip, with no LTR isolation (<bdi>, dir=ltr or U+2066/U+2069) around each host.
root_cause: src/static/app-core.js:1221 (_laneHostTitle) joins hosts as plain text, and app-boot.js:282 renders them as tip.textContent in an RTL document with no LTR isolation around each host token.
suggested_fix: Wrap each host in LTR isolates when building the title: `lane.hosts.map(h => '⁦' + h + '⁩').join(' · ')` (FSI/LRI…PDI). Plain text cannot carry <bdi>, so isolate characters are the smallest fix; tests that compare the hover's host list against the enumeration then need to strip U+2066/U+2069. Alternatively, render the host segment of the bubble in a dir=ltr span, which would require show() to accept markup.

title: 'Discover by topic', once enabled, is listed under 'Runs on every collection pass:', though SECURITY.md says it is strictly user-triggered and never part of the scheduler
repro: Settings > Advanced > Safety & at-risk use > tick 'Allow topic-discovery queries to DuckDuckGo', then open the popup with the plane icon.
expected: The popup's heading states the lane's real trigger, which is user-triggered (SECURITY.md Discover by topic row: 'Strictly user-triggered: never part of ingestion, the scheduler, or any default path').
actual: 'Discover by topic' appears under 'Runs on every collection pass:' next to the pass/ride-along lanes. It over-discloses rather than hides, but the consent surface and the security notes disagree.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/H/H-H5-en-popup-on.png; part2.json H5.popup_groups_on; src/static/app-core.js:1144-1166 (an opt-in lane whose setting is on returns the 'on' state) and 1263-1265 (the 'on' bucket is rendered under 'Runs on every collection pass:'); src/static/net-hosts.js:173-180 (trigger 'opt-in').
root_cause: src/static/app-core.js:1144-1166 (_laneState) returns _NET_STATE_ON for any 'opt-in' lane whose switch is on. app-core.js:1263-1265 renders the 'on' bucket under 'Runs on every collection pass:'. src/static/net-hosts.js topic-discovery entry has trigger 'opt-in', which is shared with the custody lane even though their runtime triggers differ.
suggested_fix: Give the topic-discovery lane in net-hosts.js an optional field such as "whenOn": "ask", and in _laneState return _NET_STATE_ASK instead of _NET_STATE_ON when the switch reads on and lane.whenOn === 'ask'. The lane then appears under 'Only when you ask for it:' when enabled and under 'Switched off right now:' when disabled. Document the field in net-hosts.js's header and pin both states in tests/net_lane_state_node_test.js.

repro: Default transparent mode: open the popup and read the 'Local AI install & weights' lane's hover text (in the DOM, since the bubble is not visible), then compare with the Local AI row's Transport column in Help > Security.

Add the new key to all 12 locales, and extend net_lane_transport_node_test.js to pin the mixed lane's direct and unknown lines.

title: French: the colon of 'Votre machine présente ces adresses réseau locales :' wraps alone onto its own line in the popup
repro: Switch to Français at 1440 px and open the popup.
expected: French punctuation spacing uses a no-break space, so ':' stays with its word.
actual: The ':' sits alone on the second line. fr.json uses a plain U+0020 before ':' in this and the other popup headings.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/H/H-H7-fr.png; src/static/locales/fr.json keys 'Your machine presents these local network addresses:' / 'Where this will let the app connect:' / 'Runs on every collection pass:' (the character before ':' is 0x20).
root_cause: src/static/locales/fr.json, value of key 'Your machine presents these local network addresses:' (and 521 other values): a breakable U+0020 before ':' where French typography requires a no-break space (U+00A0 or U+202F).
suggested_fix: Replace ' :' with ' :' (or U+202F) in that fr.json value. A one-time mechanical pass over fr.json does the same for ' :', ' ;', ' !' and ' ?' app-wide, and an i18n check can keep plain-space colons from coming back.

title: Off-row, seen incidentally: the Home at-a-glance strip keeps English labels in fr and ar
repro: Switch to Français or العربية and look at the Home strip behind the popup.
expected: Chrome strings are translated in all 12 locales.
actual: 'KEYWORDS', 'COMMODITY PRICES', 'ARTICLE LINKS', 'MENTIONED DATES', 'SOURCES QUALIFIED', 'SOURCES PENDING', 'SOURCES CANDIDATES', 'Automatic collection:' and 'stopped' stay English. The cause was not located, because it is outside this row.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/H/H-H7-fr.png, H-H7-ar.png (top strip).
root_cause: (1) Permanent: src/static/app-home.js:21-25 HOME_STAT_LABELS has no entries for sources_qualified, sources_pending or sources_candidates (emitted by src/api/database.py:110-112). homeStatLabel (app-home.js:26-29) therefore falls back to the lowercase 'sources qualified', etc., which is not a key in any locale. (2) Lag: #home-stats sits in a [data-i18n-dyn] subtree the DOM walker skips (i18n.js:~60). The oo:langchange handler (app-boot.js:128-135) repaints the strip only when it is showing the read failure, never real stats, and boot can render before OOI18N.ready, so labels wait for refreshHomeLive's 15 s poll (app-home.js:844).
suggested_fix: Add sources_qualified: 'Sources qualified', sources_pending: 'Sources pending' and sources_candidates: 'Source candidates' to HOME_STAT_LABELS, with keys in all 12 locales. Keep the last payload and repaint the strip from it in the oo:langchange handler and on OOI18N.ready, the same pattern renderHomeWikiFigure(cached) already uses.

title: Stage-4 row freezes at run end, then reads 'could not be read' on every reopen and after a restart, even while the re-index runs (Q204/Q205)
repro: Import four uncertified (pre-R24) backups at K = 3 with the dialog open and wait until the run ends. Then close and reopen Import…; also relaunch mid-drain, unlock, and open Import… while Processes shows the re-index running.
expected: Row 4 counts the re-index from the resume-status endpoint ('resuming re-index — X of Y' / 'N articles left to re-index'), and the third line reads 'Analytics are still catching up: …' until stage 4 is done, including after a reopen or a restart.
actual: At the end row 4 froze at '3,600 articles left to re-index' while the real backlog was 4,800 and draining (task manager 500 → 1000 / 4800). On every reopen, and after the restart while the drain was running, row 4 read 'could not be read' and the third line 'Whether analytics have caught up could not be read.', unchanged 4 s later.
evidence: I-I7-reopen-en.png, I-I9-import-after-restart-en.png, I-I8-taskmanager-en.png, events.jsonl (I7_all_done, I7_reopen_4s, I9_import_dialog_3s). src/static/app-backup.js:762 (reopen nulls _uxImRx), 1233-1251 (read only inside a running-queue tick; chain stops at terminal), 1697-1705 (_uxImReattach renders without reading).
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:1238-1248: _uxImTickQueue is the only reader of /reindex-backlog/resume/status. It is paced to 5 s, so the terminal tick usually skips the read. At :1253 it stops the chain on any terminal queue state, so stage 4 is never read again once the run ends. The drain only starts after the run's window closes (import_queue.py _run, around line 520). openUnifiedImport clears the read (:762, _uxImRx = null). _uxImReattach (:1697-1703) then renders with it null and arms the chain only when state === 'running' (:1702). A finished or interrupted run, including the post-boot auto-resume, can therefore only render 'could not be read' (_uxImReindexBits :1511).
suggested_fix: Decouple stage 4 from the queue's run state. On reattach and on the terminal tick, read resume/status unpaced before rendering. While the dialog is open and rx.state is 'running' or the backlog is above 0, keep a 5 s stage-4-only poll alive on the same timer and generation even though the queue is terminal. Render 'resuming re-index — X of Y' from that read, and stop the poll when rx is idle with a backlog of 0.

title: '✓ Analytics are complete' and row 4 'complete' are shown at the START of an import, before anything is merged (Q203)
repro: On an install with no re-index backlog, start any corpus import and read the dialog in the first seconds.
expected: Q203: the analytics statement becomes true only after stage 4; it must not read ✓ complete while the import has not merged anything.
actual: Row 4 reads '4. Re-index the imported articles — complete' and the third line '✓ Analytics are complete — every imported article is indexed.' at 0/4 imported. Seen in both four-backup runs.
evidence: I-I4-running-en.png (and run1/I-I4-running-en.png); src/static/app-backup.js:1510-1529 (_uxImReindexBits: backlog 0 → 'complete'), 1553-1564 (_uxImStatements reads only the backlog).
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:1561-1569: _uxImStatements decides the third statement from rx.backlog.articles_pending alone, and :1526 (_uxImReindexBits) returns 'complete' when left === 0. Neither checks that the run's items are committed or that stages 1-3 are finished. The first two statements are gated on `saved` (:1553), but this one is not.
suggested_fix: Gate the ✓ on `saved` (every item done or skipped), on the run no longer running (state !== 'running', so stage 3 is finished), and on rx.state !== 'running' with a backlog of 0. Until then show a pending bullet such as '• Analytics are complete once the re-index (stage 4) finishes', with row 4 reading 'not started'. The new string needs ×12 locales.

title: Reopening the Import dialog is not a fresh page: the previous run's header, stage rows, statements and per-backup rows re-render under 'Last import' (R1/Q201)
repro: Finish any import, close the dialog (or restart the app), and reopen Settings → Data & backup → Import….
expected: One quiet line 'Last import · <date> · N articles · open report' and nothing else (index.html comment at #ux-imp-last; Q201 = a).
actual: Beneath the line: '4/4 imported · 14s', the four numbered stage rows, the three statements and four per-backup 'Done' rows. After a restart it also shows row 3 'not started', and after an interrupted run the red 'interrupted … start it again.' line.
evidence: I-I7-reopen-en.png, I-I9-import-after-restart-en.png, I-I13b-after-relaunch-en.png; src/static/app-backup.js:1697-1705 (_uxImReattach renders any saved run); POST /api/backup/import-queue/clear has no frontend caller.
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:1697-1703: _uxImReattach renders ANY persisted run that has items (`if (!st || !(st.items||[]).length) return; _uxImRenderQueue(st);`), not only a running one. The server keeps the finished run in the queue file (import_queue.py _save/_load_persisted), and POST /api/backup/import-queue/clear (backup_v2.py:750, 'so the dialog can start clean') has no frontend caller.
suggested_fix: In _uxImReattach, call _uxImRenderQueue and _uxImWatchQueue only when st.state === 'running'. For any terminal state, hide #ux-imp-queue and leave only the quiet line. Alternatively, clear a finished run server-side when the dialog opens. An interrupted run with a genuinely interrupted item can keep one quiet line of its own.

title: '✓ Safe to close or update the app' is shown before the run is recorded finished; a stop during stage 3 boots into 'interrupted … start it again' and stage 3 is never resumed (Q203)
repro: Import one backup. The moment its row reads Done while stage 3 (search-index merge) still runs, which is when both ✓ lines are due, stop the app (SIGKILL used here; stage 3 was sub-second). Relaunch, unlock, open Import….
expected: After '✓ Safe to close or update the app', closing costs nothing and nothing asks to redo the import; stages 3-4 resume on the next boot.
actual: Red 'This import was interrupted when the app stopped. It cannot resume (the passphrase is never stored) — start it again.' under '1/1 imported · 27s', and row 3 'Merge the search index — not started', although the backup's 1,200 articles were committed (history row 06:18 · restore · 1,200 articles). Stage 3 is not resumed. Only the re-index auto-resumed.
evidence: I-I13b-after-relaunch-en.png, events.jsonl (I13b_kill: items done, search_index running, live 'merging the search index after the import'; I13b_dialog_after_relaunch); src/static/app-backup.js:1533-1551 (✓ lines keyed on item state), src/backup/import_queue.py:634-647 (run saved done only after _tune_after_run), 345-352 (running → interrupted on boot).
root_cause: src/backup/import_queue.py:634-647: _drive calls _tune_after_run() (stage 3) while the persisted state is still 'running', and saves the terminal state only afterwards. _load_persisted (:345-349) maps any 'running' state to 'interrupted' without checking whether every item had already committed. app-backup.js:1420 shows the 'start it again' line from st.state alone, while :1553-1560 grants the ✓ lines from item states. Nothing on boot re-runs optimize_after_bulk.
suggested_fix: In _load_persisted, when state == 'running' and no item is running, staged or queued (all done/skipped/error), restore the run as 'done' with tuning not done instead of 'interrupted', and schedule optimize_after_bulk once off the startup path (or run it at the next run's end). On the UI side, show the 'start it again' line only when some item's state is 'interrupted'.

title: The dialog's checkpoint sentence ignores the stored 'Backups per save point' until a run starts
repro: Settings → Data & backup → set 'Backups per save point' to 1 and tab out ('Preferences saved.'), then open Import….
expected: The sentence never disagrees with the K the next run will use: 'Every backup is verified and written to your corpus as soon as it finishes.'
actual: The sentence still reads 'Verified and written to your corpus once every 3 backups — …'. /api/settings import_checkpoint_k = 1 but /import-queue/status checkpoint.k = 3.
evidence: I-I12-k1-dialog-en.png, events.jsonl I12_k1; src/static/app-backup.js:830-843; src/backup/import_queue.py:303 (K initialised to 3), 537 (re-read only at run start), 1203.
root_cause: src/backup/import_queue.py:303 initialises _checkpoint_k to CHECKPOINT_K_DEFAULT. It is re-resolved only at run start (:537, `self._checkpoint_k = import_checkpoint_k()`), and status() reports that cached value (:1203). src/static/app-backup.js:830-843 (_uxImCheckpointNote) renders status().checkpoint.k.
suggested_fix: In status(), report `import_checkpoint_k()` whenever no run is in flight (state != 'running') and keep the captured K during a run. Alternatively, have _uxImCheckpointNote read the same resolution the next run will use.

title: End-of-run result block over-counts the re-index backlog ('8,400 article(s) still to index' after a 4,800-article import)
repro: Import four distinct 1,200-article uncertified backups at K = 3 with the dialog open until the run ends.
expected: The indexing caveat states the real pending count (4,800, the drain's own total).
actual: 'Indexing continues in the background: 8,400 article(s) still to index.' The block sums each committed item's whole-backlog snapshot (3,600 at the group save + 4,800 at backup 4).
evidence: events.jsonl I7_all_done (summary) vs I8_samples (total 4800); src/static/app-backup.js:2232-2241 (pend += r.articles_pending per item).
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:2232-2237 sums `r.articles_pending` across items. src/backup/volume_job.py:95-110 (hand_off_reindex) fills that field from reindex_backlog(), the WHOLE corpus backlog at that moment rather than this item's contribution, so each committed item's snapshot already includes the earlier ones.
suggested_fix: Do not sum snapshots of one quantity. Use the latest committed item's value (or the max), or better, read /reindex-backlog/resume/status once when rendering the block. Keep the 'could not be read' branch when none is readable.

title: Held backups leave no persisted report; history and the 'Last import' line show only per-report counts of a multi-backup run
repro: Import four distinct backups at K = 3, reopen the dialog, then open Settings → Data & backup → Import history.
expected: The persisted record, which R1 makes the only home of the detail, accounts for what each backup brought, and the Last import line says what the import added.
actual: Only two history rows (backups 3 and 4), each '1,200 articles'. Backup 3's row omits the 2,400 articles of backups 1–2 that its save committed, and 'Last import' reads '1,200 articles' for a 4,800-article import. With cumulative backups (run 1) it read '0 articles' for a run that grew the corpus by 933. The report also names no backup folder/path, and both reports are headed '(oo-backup-3)'.
evidence: I-I10-history-en.png, I-I10-report-en.png, run1/I-I7-reopen-en.png; src/backup/merge.py:6276-6292 vs 6700-6706 (report written only on the commit path).
root_cause: src/backup/merge.py:6276-6292: on hold_after_merge, run_restore returns the report before the commit path, and persist_import_report runs only at :6700-6706 on the commit path, with that item's own plan. src/backup/import_queue.py:822 (_commit_group) commits the held items without persisting a report for them. Nothing adds the item path to the report.
suggested_fix: In _commit_group (or _after_item when a group commits), persist each held item's report once its checkpoint lands, marked committed-at-checkpoint, and add the source path/label to every persisted report. Alternatively, persist one run-level report that aggregates the items, and have the 'Last import' line read the run total.

title: Verify pressed during a running import hijacks the one poll chain and freezes the run's rows
repro: Start a single-backup import; while its row reads 'Running · … stage 1 of 4', press Verify once and watch for 30 s.
expected: Q206/R2: no competing messages, and the run's rows keep updating.
actual: POST /v2/volumes/verify 409. 'Verifying…' plus 'Verify: Merging (additive)… / Committing… · phase 11 of 18' then describe the import's own restore. The header and rows froze at '0/1 imported', 'Running · 0s · stage 1 of 4' for 30 s after the import had finished, and the result was 'No verification report was returned.'. Close/reopen restored the rows.
evidence: I-I13a-verify-pressed-en.png, I-I13a-after30s-en.png, i13a_samples.jsonl; src/static/app-backup.js:900-904 + 1137-1147 (409 'running' treated as a started verify), 1167-1178.
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:1137-1146 (_uxImStartGuarded) treats ANY live volumes job as proof that its own start landed. After the 409 it reads /v2/volumes/status, finds the import's restore job 'running' and falls through, so _uxImVerify (:896-900) calls _uxImWatchVerify (:1167-1178). That switches the single chain's subject away from 'queue', and nothing re-arms the queue watch when the verify promise settles.
suggested_fix: Check the job's own kind or op in _uxImStartGuarded (accept only a live verify job) so a 409 from a running restore surfaces as 'an import is running'. Also disable the Verify button while the queue is running, and re-arm _uxImWatchQueue after a verify settles if the queue is still running.

title: Staged header line re-animates every second and overlaps the 'N/4 imported' header (R2 blink/overlap)
repro: Import ≥ 2 backups at K = 3 and watch the dialog header while a backup reads 'Merged — not yet saved'.
expected: No blinking or overlapping status text (R2).
actual: The 'Merged, not yet saved: N — …' line is an inline <span class="note">, whose .note rule gives it 11px padding, background, shadow and a 0.22 s slide-in animation. The header HTML includes the elapsed seconds, so it is rewritten each 1 s tick and the animation replays every second (animationstart at 6255 and 7271 ms). The box visibly covers the '0/4 imported · 7s' line.

title: Reopened export panel names an OLDER export and reports that verified corpus backup as 'Not verified' with 'no corpus'

expected: The reopened dialog shows the LAST completed export (folder B) with its own facts, or at least, for whichever folder it names, the same facts that folder's BACKUP_SUMMARY.md holds (backup_v2.py's own docstring: 'a reopened dialog and the file on the drive cannot disagree').

Folder A's BACKUP_SUMMARY.md says Verified, 4 volumes, corpus encrypted, two licence lines. GET /api/backup/export-summary?dir=<A> returns corpus_included=false, verify.state=unknown.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/J/shots/J-J7-reopen-after-corpus-only-en.png; /tmp/claude-0/walk/J/results/j7.json (reopen_panel_after_two; job_status: volumes job dest=B, folder job dest=A). Cause: src/static/app-backup.js:66-80 lets the folder job's done state override the volume job's unconditionally ('the more recent state'), which is false when a later export had no large-data phase; src/backup/export_summary.py:175-179 then drops every corpus fact because the in-memory volume status belongs to a different folder.
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:66-80 (_uxShowLastCompletedExportSummary): a done folder-job status overwrites a done volumes-job status unconditionally (line 76, 'the more recent state to show'). That is false when a later export had no large-data phase, because the folder manager keeps an older dest. Then src/backup/export_summary.py:177-179 discards the volume summary because its dest differs, and line 202 turns 'summary not in memory for this folder' into corpus_included=false. The panel (app-backup.js:141-146, 196) and the verify sentence render that as 'no corpus was selected' plus a red 'Not verified'.
suggested_fix: (1) Client: in _uxShowLastCompletedExportSummary, let the folder status win only if its dest equals the volumes dest (the same export) or the volume job holds no completed backup. Otherwise the two are different exports and the later one must win, which needs a finished_at timestamp in both managers' status() and a pick-the-latest rule. (2) export_facts: stop equating 'no in-memory summary for this folder' with 'no corpus selected'. Base corpus_included on volumes.json existing in the folder. When the in-memory facts belong to another export, return an explicit 'facts no longer in memory; see BACKUP_SUMMARY.md' state rather than verify 'unknown' plus 'none — no corpus was selected'.

evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/J/exports-reload/202609261816_OpenOmniscience_Backup/ (listing); /tmp/claude-0/walk/J/results/reloadmid.json; /tmp/claude-0/walk/J/shots/J-reloadmid-reopen-en.png. Cause: only the page's _uxRun sends POST /api/backup/export-summary, at its very end (src/static/app-backup.js:673); the reopen path (62-107) only GETs facts, and the GET response carries no summary_path (src/api/backup_v2.py:651-658).
root_cause: BACKUP_SUMMARY.md is written only by the page: the POST /api/backup/export-summary at the tail of _uxRun (src/static/app-backup.js:673), inside the closure that a reload destroys. The reopen path (app-backup.js:94-104) only GETs facts. export_summary_read (src/api/backup_v2.py:651-658) returns no summary_path or exists flag, so the panel cannot say the file is missing.

In VolumeJobManager._run_backup, write it right after kept['verify'] is set (src/backup/volume_job.py:393), from export_facts(destp, volume_status=self.status()). Add a Chromium test that hovers a #net-consent lane and asserts the bubble's centre pixel is not covered by the dialog.

evidence:

src/static/app-ai-tools.js:496 (overlayMerge catch → _apiErrorMessage(e)) and :444 (overlayExport catch, same shape). These fetch() paths throw new Error(msg) without .detail.

title: The task manager (/tasks) always shows ONLINE: the plane never fills, and the offline title and the 'Airplane mode' state never appear
repro: Boot normally (airplane mode). Click the top-bar 'Tasks & system' icon, or open /tasks. Hover the plane. Or: boot with OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1 (online), open /tasks and click its plane once.
expected: While offline: plane filled and red, title 'Offline (airplane mode) — click to go online in the app; you'll be asked to confirm first.' (translated live), summary 'Airplane mode'. After the offline click, the same.
actual: While the server is offline (/api/system/network and /api/scheduler/status both online:false): plane hollow and not red, title 'Online — click to go offline (airplane mode); every new network request will be refused.', summary 'Idle'. Seen on 3 retries (6/12/20 s) and in fr/ar/zh. After the offline click the POST succeeds and #tm-conn shows the offline toast, but the plane, title and summary stay online-looking for 12 s+. The safety control's FILL (invariant #14) misstates the state, and Q1126's offline half is never shown.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/T/T-T5-tasks-while-offline-en-fr-ar-zh.png, /tmp/claude-0/walk/T/T-T8-tasks-after-offline-click-en.png, walk1b.json T5_retries (api_activity_has_online:false). Cause: src/static/taskmanager.html:522-524 (and :392 renderSchedule) read act.online from GET /api/scheduler/activity. src/scheduler/runner.py:2282-2308 builds that payload from self.status() without 'online'; only src/api/scheduler.py:130 (_status_payload, used by the /status responses) adds it. So act.online is undefined and `act.online !== false` paints online.
root_cause: src/static/taskmanager.html:522-524 (renderSummary: `_tmOnline = act ? (act.online !== false) : null`) and :392 (renderSchedule: `offline = a.online === false`) read `online` from GET /api/scheduler/activity. That route (src/api/scheduler.py:271-277) returns `get_scheduler().activity(db)`. src/scheduler/runner.py:2282-2308 builds that payload from `self.status()` plus plan and rates, and never adds `online`. Only `_status_payload()` (src/api/scheduler.py:123-130), which the /status, start, stop and resume responses use, adds `status["online"] = not kill_switch_active()`. So `act.online` is undefined and `undefined !== false` paints online. The task manager's own header comment (taskmanager.html:19-20) documents that /activity carries `online`, so the endpoint drifted from its documented contract. test_repo_invariants.py:5985 only checks for the string 'a.online === false' in the HTML, so the missing key was never caught.
suggested_fix: src/api/scheduler.py scheduler_activity: `from src.ingest import kill_switch_active; out = get_scheduler().activity(db); out["online"] = not kill_switch_active(); return out` (the same line _status_payload uses). Add a behavioural test that GET /api/scheduler/activity carries a boolean `online` equal to `not kill_switch_active()`. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/T-recheck/T-recheck-tasks-offline-en.png, T-recheck-tasks-after-offline-click-en.png, T-recheck-tasks-schedule-offline-en.png, T-recheck-tasks-offline-with-online-key-en.png (fix simulated), recheck1.json defect1_*, recheck2.json fixsim_*.

title: NEW (found during recheck): in RTL (ar) at desktop width, the net-coach covers the top-bar #tm-open, #rate-toggle, #wiki-toggle and #llm
root_cause: src/static/app-core.js:1024-1026. The 'prefer to the right of the button' branch assumes the button sits at the right edge, which only holds in LTR. It sets `top = b.top + b.height/2 - h/2`. For a coach about 135 px tall next to a 34 px button at y 14-48, that is negative, and the clamp at :1043 raises it to 8 px, inside the top-bar row. That is the same collapse-into-the-top-bar mechanism the :1027-1036 comment describes for the old 'above' placement. In RTL the plane sits at x 186-220, so the branch is taken, and the coach lands on the controls to the right of the plane.
suggested_fix: Never place the coach inside the top-bar row. Either always use the existing 'below the union of the protected buttons' placement, which works in either direction, or keep the side branch only when `top >= guardBottom + gap`. The smallest change: compute guardBottom before the if, and require `b.top + b.height/2 - h/2 >= guardBottom + gap` in the side-branch condition. Also add '#rate-toggle', '#wiki-toggle' and '#llm' to the guard list, and add an RTL case to the net-coach elementFromPoint regression test. title: The first-launch 'Where should your corpus live?' screen never appears, because the lock gate blocks its endpoint
repro: Point OO_DATA_DIR at an empty folder and boot with the console script (no passphrase variable). Open the app, pick English, tick the box and press 'Accept and continue'.
expected: The screen 'Where should your corpus live?' (#view-datadir), with 'Use the app's own data folder' selected, then 'Create your corpus passphrase'.
actual: Two independent fresh launches went straight to 'Create your corpus passphrase'. While the state is 'fresh', GET /api/system/data-location returns 503 {'detail':'the database is locked: unlock it first'}; unlock.html reads that as offerable=false and silently skips the step. The choice of data folder is therefore unreachable at the only moment it is offered.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/U/empty.log has 'GET /api/system/data-location HTTP/1.1 503'. src/api/unlock.py:77-93: ALLOWED_WHILE_LOCKED does not list /api/system/data-location or /data-location/check. src/api/unlock.py:70-71: app_is_locked() is True for 'fresh'. src/api/main.py:753-763: the lock gate. src/static/unlock.html:340-345: the silent skip. tests/test_data_location.py:283-292 mounts the router without the middleware, so the tests cannot see this. The checker's note (1) assumed the opposite (that the screen shows on every fresh launch).
root_cause: src/api/unlock.py:75-93: ALLOWED_WHILE_LOCKED does not list /api/system/data-location. unlock.py:70-71: app_is_locked() is True for 'fresh'. src/api/main.py:751-763: the _lock_gate middleware answers 503 for every other path. src/static/unlock.html:340-345: legalToDataLocation() parses the 503 body, where info.offerable is undefined, and silently calls legalToPassphrase(). tests/test_data_location.py:283-292 mounts the router on a bare FastAPI() without the middleware, so no test can see this.
suggested_fix: Add "/api/system/data-location" to ALLOWED_WHILE_LOCKED. The prefix match covers GET, POST /check and POST, and both POSTs already refuse with 409 unless the state is 'fresh', so nothing opens after a store exists. Add a test through the real src.api.main app, which runs the middleware, at state 'fresh', asserting 200 and offerable:true. Optionally make unlock.html treat a non-2xx answer as an error rather than as 'not offerable'. Also decide on unlock.html:336-339: its comment says an explicit OO_DATA_DIR skips the step, but the handler's offerable ignores explicit_override, and the existing test pins offerable to 'fresh' only.

title: Calendar directory hint advertises ~500 multi-provider feeds including religions, elections, space and astronomy that the directory does not serve
repro: On the unlocked seeded instance: Settings → Advanced → 'Calendar directory'. Open the Kind menu, or type 'Christian' or 'Astronomy' in Filter.
expected: Kind = religion lists 8 families; Kind = science includes 'Astronomy — eclipses, moons, solstices, meteor showers'.
actual: Kind offers only all, civic, community and holidays, across 241 feeds; no religion or astronomy family matches any filter. The hint still reads 'A bundled directory of ~500 public calendar feeds (country holidays, religions, elections, UN days, space, astronomy)'. The families are in the YAML, but on screen they are already gone.
evidence: src/events/feeds.py:58-60 (_DEAD_DEFAULT_HOSTS), :96 (the feed filter), :99-102 (a family with no feed left drops out). configs/calendar_feeds.yml:3135-3230: every religion feed is on calendar.google.com or www.webcal.guru; 3285-3297: the astronomy feeds are on dead or retired hosts. src/static/index.html:2724: the hint text. /api/events/feeds lists only holidays (239), civic (1) and community (1). Screenshot U-U9-directory-kinds-en.png. The filtering may be deliberate; what disagrees with it is the gate text and the hint.
root_cause: src/static/index.html:2724-2725: static hint text was not updated when the 2026-07-10 B7 load-time filter (src/events/feeds.py:58-102) cut the directory to 241 single-provider families.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the hint to describe what load_families() actually serves: about 240 country-holiday feeds plus UN days and one community calendar, one provider each. Add one line saying that feeds whose hosts' robots.txt refuses them are withheld. Alternatively, render the counts from /api/events/feeds. Key the new strings ×12.

title: The Help page scrolls sideways by 406 px at 375 px width
repro: Load the app at 375x812 and press the top-bar '?' button.
expected: No sideways scroll (scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0), as on the other row U surfaces.
actual: scrollWidth - clientWidth = 406. The User Manual's install <code> line reaches x=829, the document-list buttons are 744 px wide, and body text is cut at the right edge.
evidence: Screenshot U-375-fresh-help-en.png; probe375fresh.json. src/static/app.css:1675 sets '.doc-layout { grid-template-columns:1fr; }', and a 1fr column still widens to fit the unbroken <pre> line.
root_cause: src/static/app.css:1622 (grid-template-columns:230px 1fr) and :1675 (grid-template-columns:1fr at ≤600px). A 1fr track has an 'auto' minimum, so it grows to the grid item's min-content, which includes the unbreakable <pre> line. The pre's overflow-x:auto (app.css:1648) does not lower the min-content contribution of its non-scrolling grid-item ancestor.
suggested_fix: Use minmax(0,1fr) in both rules (230px minmax(0,1fr) at desktop, minmax(0,1fr) at ≤600px), or add .doc-layout > * { min-width:0 }. The existing .prose pre { overflow-x:auto } then scrolls inside the box.

title: Home's at-a-glance strip stays in the previous language after a switch, and three of its counters are never translated
repro: On Home in English, switch the top bar to Français or العربية and read the strip above the briefing.
expected: The strip changes to the new language at once, like the card below it.
actual: It stays English until the next background refresh, about 20 s in fr. In the ar screenshot of U1, 'Your library is empty — head to Collect…' and 'Automatic collection: stopped · Your corpus stays on this machine…' are English. After a reload in fr, the strip was still English 5 s later. Even after the refresh, 'sources qualified', 'sources pending' and 'sources candidates' stay English, and 'as of 08:11 PM' keeps the English time format.
evidence: probe_strip.json, probe_strip2.json; screenshots U-U1-home-ar.png and U-U1-home-strip-fr-seeded.png. src/static/app-home.js:21-29: these labels fall back to t(k.replace(/_/g,' ')), a key no language file has and the i18n check cannot see. src/static/app-home.js:57-62: the strip is inside [data-i18n-dyn]. src/static/app-boot.js:55-135: the language-switch repaint list does not include the strip.
root_cause: src/static/app-home.js:21-29: HOME_STAT_LABELS lacks sources_qualified/sources_pending/sources_candidates, and the fallback t(k.replace(/_/g,' ')) has no key in any locale. app-home.js:46: toLocaleTimeString([], …) uses the browser locale, not the UI language. index.html:247: the strip sits inside [data-i18n-dyn], so the i18n walker skips it (i18n.js:58). app-boot.js:41-135: the one oo:langchange listener repaints the strip's Wikipedia figure and failure line, but never calls renderHomeStats or renderHomeStatus. So the strip waits for refreshHomeLive (app-home.js:844).
suggested_fix: Keep the last /api/database/stats payload and scheduler running flag. In the oo:langchange listener, call renderHomeStats(cached.counts, cached) and renderHomeStatus(cachedRunning), without a fetch. Add the three labels to HOME_STAT_LABELS and key them ×12. Pass the UI locale (uiLangCode()) to toLocaleTimeString.

title: The newsletter caveat has no hover mark and does not open the shared hover bubble
repro: Settings → Data & backup → import .eml files so that at least one is filed → hover the amber caveat.
expected: Per invariant #17, the caveat is marked (dotted underline) and hovering it opens #oo-tip with the explanation of how filing is decided.
actual: #nl-attach-caveat has only the class card-caveat, and #oo-tip stays hidden; the counts beside it do open the bubble. Only the browser's plain native tooltip would appear.
evidence: main_U7.json: u7.hover_caveat has tip.vis false with the title present; u7.hover_count has tip.vis true. At page load the element has no title. src/static/app-settings.js:1424 sets .title later, on an element that already exists. src/static/app-boot.js:268-275 marks only elements that have a title at boot or are added later; it does not watch attribute changes.
root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:268-275: ooTipInit marks [title] elements once at boot and afterwards only for childList addedNodes. It never observes attribute changes. src/static/app-settings.js:1424 sets .title on the static #nl-attach-caveat (index.html:1991, which has no title at load). The textContent write at :1423 adds only a text node, which the observer skips because of the nodeType===1 check.
suggested_fix: Generic fix: observe attributes as well, with {childList:true, subtree:true, attributes:true, attributeFilter:['title']}, and mark m.target on attribute mutations. That closes the gap for every surface that sets .title later. The show()/hide() title swaps only re-add a class that is already there. Local fix: add classList.add('oo-tip-target') in loadNewsletterAttach.

title: In the newsletter source rows the count runs into the name ('BBC News1', 'some-unknown-press.org disabled2')
repro: After an import that files newsletters, read the rows under 'Automatically filed newsletters: N'.
expected: The source name and its count shown apart, name on the left and count on the right.
actual: The name, the 'disabled' tag and the count run together: 'BBC News1', 'some-unknown-press.org disabled2'. Same in ar: 'معطّل2'.
evidence: Screenshots U-U7-attach-en.png and U-U7-attach-ar-375.png. src/static/app-settings.js:1415-1419 builds rows as a .vr div with no separator between name and count. src/static/app.css:835 styles .vr only inside .vitals-pop.
root_cause:
src/static/app-settings.js:1413-1417 builds each row as
name…count
with no separator. The only .vr rules are scoped to .vitals-pop (src/static/app.css:835-839), so outside the task-manager popover the row is an unstyled block.
suggested_fix: Add a scoped rule such as #nl-attach-body .vr { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; gap:10px; }, which mirrors the .vitals-pop .vr rule. Alternatively, put a ' · ' between the span and the <b>.

title: Two first-run dialogs open on top of each other on a fresh install, in an unpredictable order
repro: Fresh folder → language → legal → create passphrase → the app opens at /?wikiwizard=1.
expected: One first-run dialog at a time.
actual: #wiki-wizard and #guide-wizard are both open. The one underneath cannot be clicked until the top one is closed, and which one was on top differed between the two runs.
evidence: u1.json: dialogs_after_entry {wiki: true, guide: true} and dismiss_order; screenshot U-U1-entry-dialogs-en.png. src/static/app-boot.js:555-558 opens the Wikipedia dialog and src/static/app-backup.js:2708 opens the guide; nothing stops both opening at once.
root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:555-558 calls openWikiWizard() when ?wikiwizard=1 is present. That function is async: it awaits /api/wiki/languages and /api/scheduler/config, then calls showModal (src/static/app-sources.js:1323-1350). Independently, app-boot.js:213 calls checkEmptyCorpus(), which awaits /api/database/stats and then calls openGuide() (src/static/app-backup.js:2705-2709 → app-core.js:785-789 showModal). Neither checks whether the other is open or pending, so the order depends on which fetch resolves first.
suggested_fix: Sequence the two. In checkEmptyCorpus, when ?wikiwizard=1 is present or #wiki-wizard is open, defer openGuide() to the wiki wizard's 'close' event (dlg.addEventListener('close', openGuide, {once:true})), so exactly one first-run dialog is open at a time and the order is deterministic.

title: The Price chart's axis label and the Agenda moon hovers keep the previous language after a switch; the moon method sentence is English in every language
repro: Open Dy's Price subtab (or the Agenda month view) in English, then switch to fr, ar or zh without reopening it.
expected: Text drawn into the chart and the hover follows the switch, like the heading next to it.
actual: The label stays 'Price USD/kg' in fr, ar and zh, even after selecting the Price subtab again; opening it fresh in fr gives 'Prix USD/kg'. Moon hovers stay 'Last quarter moon …' after the switch, while a fresh fr render gives 'Dernier quartier …'. The Meeus method and accuracy text after the dash is English in every language.
evidence: extra.json and w375.json (the probes). src/static/app-analysis.js:538 bakes t9('Price') into the chart when it is drawn. src/static/app-agenda.js:1252 and 1311 build the hover text when the grid is drawn, from the server's method text. Neither is redrawn on a language switch.
root_cause: src/static/app-analysis.js:538 bakes t9('Price') into the overlay SVG when it is drawn. src/static/app-agenda.js:1252 (month) and :1311 (week) build the title and weekday names once, at render time. They concatenate the server's moon.method and moon.acc, English constants _METHOD/_ACCURACY in src/events/astronomy.py, without t(). None of these renderers is registered in the oo:langchange listener (src/static/app-boot.js:41-135). The i18n gates cannot see server-sent strings.
suggested_fix: Register the agenda grid re-render and the price-overlay redraw in the one oo:langchange listener, redrawing from retained payloads with no fetch, as _anRepaintXLang and _renderPatternsGate already do. Pass moon.method, moon.acc, season.method and season.acc through t(). Key the few fixed Meeus method and accuracy strings ×12, the same way loadNewsletterAttach already does t(d.caveat).

title: The Commodities chart is not redrawn when the window gets narrower
repro: Open Commodities at 1440 px, narrow the window to 375 px without reloading, and go back to Commodities.
expected: The chart refits and nothing scrolls sideways.
actual: A 937-px canvas remains and the page scrolls sideways by 562 px. Loading the page directly at 375 px is fine.
evidence: w375.json: w375.commodities has hscroll 562 and a 937-px CANVAS as the widest element. probe375fresh.json: markets.hscroll 0.
root_cause: src/static/app-markets.js:1756-1775: ooChart measures el.clientWidth once and sizes the canvas in fixed px (W = min(avail, 900)). The only ResizeObserver (:1758-1766) handles the not-yet-laid-out zero-width case and disconnects after the first render, so nothing refits the chart when its host narrows.
suggested_fix: Keep one ResizeObserver per chart host and re-run ooChart(el, seriesList, opts) when el.clientWidth differs from the drawn W by more than a few px, with a debounce and without refetching. Alternatively, give the canvas max-width:100% and map pointer events through getBoundingClientRect.
